title: A run pushes nothing until closeout, so an interrupted run loses everything
description:
THE MOST EXPENSIVE ARCHITECTURAL GAP FOUND SO FAR. Forensics on run_f15efdfb ($49.80, 4.4 hours) show it was NOT thrashing — it was productively working the whole of epic 72y across seven ticks in parallel worktrees: gm5, 201, 5jo, 5qj, 3nh, 09w and iit, editing real test files. Roughly $7 per tick of implementation.

None of it survived. The run pushed nothing, so when the container was destroyed to stop the spend, four hours of work on seven ticks vanished.

D4 says tracker writes happen in the orchestrator sandbox checkout and are pushed as commits on a run branch, merged at closeout. The design even anticipates the failure: "if the run dies permanently, its .tick/ state is on the pushed run branch — durable, recoverable, and mergeable". That property does not hold, because nothing pushes until closeout. A run that does not REACH closeout has never pushed at all.

Fix: push the run branch incrementally — at minimum after each wave integrates, ideally after each tick's worker branch merges. It is the run's own branch, so pushing early costs nothing and risks nothing; the merge to the default branch still waits for closeout and the PR+CI gate. Then a killed, evicted or budget-stopped run leaves recoverable work, exactly as the design claims.

Two supporting facts from the same incident:
- The harness output stream froze at offset 3014 for over four hours while the run was demonstrably working. From outside, productive work and a hang were indistinguishable, which is what made killing it look correct. Whatever buffers that stream must flush on a timer, not only at turn boundaries.
- Killing the container was the only thing that stopped the spend (gyl), so the operator was forced to choose between an unstoppable run and destroying its work. With incremental push that choice stops being destructive.

2026-08-21 09:57 - runner-state: runner=claude branch=tick/tpl merged=d0f6656f
2026-08-21 09:57 - Durability is mechanical, in the container, not in a prompt (same reasoning as D14 for budgets): a keeper loop fast-forward-pushes HEAD to tick-run/<epic> every TICKS_KEEPER_INTERVAL seconds and prints a heartbeat, so a working run and a hung one are distinguishable from outside. Two invariants to not regress: nothing is pushed before the run has committed something (a keeper that staked the branch at the base would make ehy's progress verdict report progress no run made), and a run branch that does not descend from this boot's base is left untouched — that run pushes to tick-run/<epic>-<run id> beside it. Never --force: a rejected push is retried, because forcing over a ref this run does not own would lose exactly the work the keeper exists to preserve.
acceptance_criteria: A run pushes its run branch incrementally as waves integrate; a run killed mid-epic leaves completed ticks recoverable on the remote; harness output flushes on a timer so a working run is distinguishable from a hung one.
closed_reason: Completed: a run's work now reaches origin continuously on tick-run/<epic> instead of only at closeout, so an interrupted run is recoverable rather than lost — the failure that cost seven implemented ticks when only container deletion could stop the runaway. A later boot continues a run branch that descends from its base, which is what lets a killed run's work be picked up and what lets closeout see what a dead container did.
